text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - canary `/api-inference` 5xx rate spike detected (18% over 5% threshold). Alerted at 3355000000.

alex_cheng: I see it. Any recent deploys to the canary pool?

maya_kapoor: Pushed a canary earlier from CI around 3354999900, image `registry.redwood/dev/api:2026-03-16-canary`. Only ~10% traffic.

samir_patel: looking at CI artifacts now. Build logs show `docker push` succeeded but manifest digests differ between eu-west registry and s3-backend cache. Suspect registry proxy cache poisoning.

tayla_ortega: Confirmed 5xxs are primarily 504s and a couple 500s from `model-loader` during cold-start. Might be incompatible runtime binary in that image.

alex_cheng: Ok. Priority: stop canary traffic and flip the feature flag while we assess. Can someone toggle `feature:canary_api_v2` to `off`?

maya_kapoor: On it. Running: `./ops/flags set canary_api_v2 false --env prod`

maya_kapoor: (output) `OK  feature canary_api_v2 -> false` :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Automated action: pausing canary routing for `api-inference` (policy id: rt-77). Scaling canary replicas to 0.

rachel_sre: Nice. I'll shift traffic back to stable pool `api-stable-2026-02` and watch error rates.

rachel_sre: (metric snippet) `canary 5xx: 18% -> 4.6%` within 90s of flag flip. Rolling average dropping.

samir_patel: CI artifact trace: `digest pushed: sha256:aaa111` but registry returned `sha256:bbb222` to some nodes. Proxy returned stale blob for multi-arch manifest. We should invalidate proxy cache and re-pull correct manifest.

alex_cheng: Do we have a rollback for the canary image? Either full rollback or re-push fixed artifact. I want kill-switch first (done), then rollback to the previous stable canary image if needed.

maya_kapoor: We can re-run the pipeline to rebuild and repush with enforced `--disable-cache` and pinned digest. Starting rebuild now: `bk build job/ci-api/#4578 --no-cache`

samir_patel: Also opening a ticket with registry team to investigate cache invalidation and sign manifests. I'll attach signatures from both pushes.

rachel_sre: Customer impact: CS reported increased errors in several seats using batched embeddings for ~12 minutes. Notifying top 5 affected customers with mitigation note.

alex_cheng: Good. Marking this P1 incident for postmortem. Tagging owners: @samir_patel (artifact), @maya_kapoor (CI), @rachel_sre (mitigation).

deploy-bot: Rollback plan: if rebuilt image appears healthy, we will canary redeploy with `strategy: serial` to avoid wide blast radius.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0432 created. Severity: P1. Channels: #oncall, #incidents, #customer-ops. Handoff to SRE for follow-up.

alex_cheng: Thanks everyone. Keep updates short here — if anything changes (novel 5xx pattern or traffic doesn't normalize) escalate to pager.

maya_kapoor: Rebuild completed and pushed new digest `sha256:ccc333`. Forcing pull and invalidated proxy cache at 3355000110 with `registry-tool invalidate --manifest sha256:bbb222`.

rachel_sre: Observability: health checks stable, error rate back under 1%. I'll keep monitors on for next 30 minutes.

samir_patel: Registry team confirmed root cause: race between mirrored pushes + stale CDN layer. They've scheduled a config change to assert manifest integrity.

alex_cheng: Closing immediate paging loop. We'll schedule postmortem to cover CI hardening, registry signing, and a kill-switch playbook. Thanks. :thumbsup:
